editorial:
You follow Nicoline, a criminal psychologist who starts a new job at a prison. Her newest case is Idris, a sex offender who seems reformed after five years behind bars. He is charming and confident, and despite her training, Nicoline finds herself drawn to him. The tension builds as their sessions blur the line between professional and personal, making you wonder who is really in control.

The acting is strong, especially the chemistry between the two leads. The pacing is slow but deliberate, keeping you on edge the whole time. Some viewers might find the subject matter uncomfortable, and a few scenes feel repetitive. If you enjoy psychological thrillers with complex characters, this is for you. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Nicoline and Idris's relationship reaches a breaking point. Despite warnings from colleagues, she lets her guard down, and the power dynamic shifts. Idris reveals his true manipulative nature, showing he has not really changed. Nicoline realizes she has been played, and the film ends with her confronting the consequences of crossing professional boundaries, leaving you questioning who was really in control all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers with complex characters and moral gray areas.
